ORAL ORDER (PER: THE HON'BLE MS. JUSTICE J.M.KHAZI)

The petitioner who is the sole accused has filed this petition under Section 439 of Code of Criminal Procedure (for short, 'the Cr.P.C.') to grant bail in Crime No.213/2023 for the offences punishable under Sections of 376(2)(i), 376(2)(n) of IPC and Sections 5(j)(ii), 6, 10 and 12 of POCSO Act.
2. In support of the petition, petitioner has contended that he is innocent and law abiding citizen.
He has not committed the alleged offences and he has been falsely implicated.
There are no serious allegations against him.
Only to escape from the situation, after prolonged delay complaint is filed.
It is an after thought.
The complaint averments are false and imaginary only to implicate the petitioner.
The ingredients of the offences are not attracted.
Prosecutrix is stated to be aged 14 years whereas her dental age is 16 years.
The prosecutrix NC: 2024:KHC-D:11676 and her parents are residents of Takawade village, Shirol taluk, Maharashtra, whereas petitioner is residing at Kanadal village in Raibag taluk, Belagavi.
Already investigation is completed and charge sheet is filed.

Petitioner is ready and willing to abide by any conditions that may be imposed and offer substantial surety to the satisfaction of the Trial Court and prays to allow the petition.
3.
In this petition defecto-complainant is arraigned as respondent No.2.

On due service of notice,
she has appeared through counsel.
4. Learned High Court Government Pleader submitted oral objections stating that prosecutrix and her parents are residents of Takawade village, Shirol taluk of Maharashtra.
Petitioner is a resident of Kanadal of Raibag taluk of Belagavi.
However, he used to stay in the house of his maternal uncle Laxman Yallappa Pol at Takawade and go to centering work with the parents of prosecutrix.

The mother of accused by name Chaya Kadam also used to NC: 2024:KHC-D:11676 visit her brother's house and both families were knowing each other and infact, prosecutrix used to address Chaya Kadam as aunt.
5. In this background, during May 2023, in the second week, prosecutrix went to the house of Chaya Kadam to spend summer vacation.
After staying for two months, during the last week of July, she returned to Takwade.
However, during September 2023, she informed the complainant that since four months she is not having her menstrual period.

Since her menstrual periods were not regular,
complainant did not worry about it and after she got some money, she took her to Magadum hospital, Ichalakaranji.
After conducting sonography, the doctor reveals that prosecutrix is four months pregnant.

On enquiry, prosecutrix revealed that while she was in the house of Chaya Kadam,
accused committed rape on her about four to five times promising to marry her.

sentences.text: Based on the said information, complaint was lodged.
Both prosecutrix and the accused are subjected to medical examination.
Infact, the prosecutrix underwent medical termination of pregnancy and the fetus is preserved for DNA testing.
After detailed investigation, charge sheet is filed against the petitioner for the offences punishable under Sections 376(2)(n), 376(2)(i) of IPC Sections 5(J)(ii), 6, 10 and 12 of POCSO Act.
The allegations made against the petitioner are very severe.

In the event of granting bail, he may tamper the witnesses and also abscond and thereby,
delay and defeat the proceedings and prays to dismiss the petition.
7. Learned counsel for respondent No.2 has also submitted that having regard to the severity of the allegations made, the bail application filed by the petitioner is liable to be rejected.
8. Heard arguments and perused the record.
It is pertinent to note that when the incident took place, prosecutrix was aged 14 years and was studying in 9th standard.

The allegations against the petitioner are that since he was working with the parents of the prosecutrix and his mother, Chaya Kadam was also visiting them, with that acquaintance during Summer Vacation prosecutrix stayed in the house of Chaya Kadam and petitione at Takawade for two months.
During this period, petitioner committed rape on her on 4 to 5 times.
She did not disclose this fact to her parents.
Only after she missed her regular periods, when she was taken to the hospital, it was revealed that she is pregnant and carrying a fetus of 22 weeks.
Since the pregnancy was a result of sexual assault, with the consent of the prosecutrix and her mother, the fetus was aborted and it was preserved for medical examination.
10. In this regard, the mother of the prosecutrix has lodged complaint.
On the basis of it, case is registered and investigation is taken up.
The prosecutrix as well as NC: 2024:KHC-D:11676 the petitioner/accused were subjected to medical examination.

With the permission of the Trial Court,
the blood samples of the prosecutrix and the petitioner/accused are drawn and sent for DNA examination to ascertain the paternity and maternity of the fetus.
After completing the investigation, charge sheet is filed.
DNA report is awaited.

11. The charge sheet makes out strong prima facie case against the petitioner for the offences punishable under Sections No.213/2023 for the offences punishable under Sections 376(2)(i),
376(2)(n) of IPC and Sections 5(j)(ii), 6, 10 and 12 of POCSO.
At the time of incident, the prosecutrix was aged 14 years.
Her parents are coolie workers.
They belongs to vulnerable sections of the society.

The minimum sentence prescribed for the offence punishable under Section 376 of IPC and Section 6 of POCSO Act is imprisonment for not less than twenty years, which may extend to imprisonment for life which means remainder of the natural life of that person.

The petitioner NC:
2024:KHC-D:11676 is also a coolie worker aged about 24 years.
Having regarding to the gravity of the offence, and social status of the parties, the possibility of the prosecution witnesses being threatened and tampered with cannot be ruled out.

Looking to the gravity of the punishment Shravan S/O Ashok Kadam vs The State Of Karnataka on 14 August, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/53449417/
3 prescribed, the possibility of accused absconding and thereby protracting the proceedings also cannot be ruled out.

ORDER Petition filed by the petitioner/accused in Crime No.213/2023 for the offences punishable under Sections 376(2)(i), 376(2)(n) of IPC and Sections 5(j)(ii),
6, 10 and 12 of POCSO Act is dismissed.
